digest.component_or_area: GitHub Actions CI workflow and test infrastructure
propositions: An experiment to move macOS pytest temporary trees from runner.temp to an ephemeral APFS RAM disk was rejected because measured wall times on the RAM-disk treatment runs (18m43s, 20m54s, 18m26s, 20m00s) consistently underperformed the no-RAM control (17m26s default, 20m36s job), failing to meet the predeclared retention threshold of 5% improvement.

The RAM-disk implementation exposed a secondary defect: intentionally owner-nonwritable workflow snapshot fixture directories prevented ordinary recursive basetemp cleanup, requiring explicit recursive chmod restoration before rm -rf.

A tertiary cacheprovider isolation defect was discovered where nested pytest subprocess invocations inherited the outer cacheprovider disabled state, leaking .pytest_cache entries into REPO_ROOT; restoration required adding -p no:cacheprovider to the nested process.

The treatment lifecycle and experiment-only workflow contract were reverted; both default and integration pytest tiers remain routed to separate bastemps under runner.temp, and all platform/Python matrix cells, selectors, markers, worker counts, timeouts, and coverage behavior remain unchanged.

Static workflow contract tests and all existing test consumers (test_ci_workflow_parity.py, test_gate_step_tree_skew.py, test_extra_coverage_guard.py, test_worktree_python_pin.py) continued to pass without modification throughout the experiment and reversion.
The N=3000 import benchmark long pole (13.69s of 24 required git-add/git-commit pairs) remains a separate performance tracking item despite the RAM-disk hypothesis being disproven for this workload.
